title: Hitting time minus neighbor average
statement: Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $s,t$ be distinct vertices. For each vertex $v$, define $H_N(t,v)$ as the sum, over $0\le j<N$, of the probabilities that a uniformly chosen indexed-neighbor walk of length $j$ from $v$ avoids $t$ at every visited vertex, including its endpoint. Write $A H_N(t,s)=\frac{1}{D}\sum_{i=0}^{D-1}H_N(t,G.\mathrm{nbr}(s,i))$ for the average of this quantity over the indexed neighbors of $s$. Then $H_N(t,s)-A H_N(t,s)\le 1$ for every integer $N\ge0$.
hypotheses_covered: $G$ is a finite regular multigraph of degree $D$
